from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Knowledge: Snell's Law and Light", 
                         ["Light always follows the path of least time.", 
                          "Snell's Law describes how light bends between media.", 
                          "Light curves to spend more time in faster zones."])

        # Colors for elements
        ray_color = "#FFFFFF"
        snell_color = "#FFFF00"
        layer_color = "#888888"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ray_color))
        
        # Setup the interface and normal for Snell's Law
        # Interface is between Row C and Row D
        y_c = self.grid["C3"][1]
        y_d = self.grid["D3"][1]
        interface_y = (y_c + y_d) / 2
        
        # Normal line at the center of the visual area (between Col 3 and 4)
        x_normal = (self.grid["C3"][0] + self.grid["C4"][0]) / 2
        
        interface = Line(start=[0.5, interface_y, 0], end=[5.5, interface_y, 0], color=GRAY)
        normal = DashedLine(start=[x_normal, 2.5, 0], end=[x_normal, -2.8, 0], color=GRAY_A)
        
        # Light ray starting from A1, hitting interface at normal, and entering second medium
        p_start = self.grid["B1"]
        p_hit = np.array([x_normal, interface_y, 0])
        p_end = self.grid["E5"]
        
        ray_part1 = Line(p_start, p_hit, color=ray_color)
        ray_part2 = Line(p_hit, p_end, color=ray_color)
        
        self.play(Create(interface), Create(normal))
        self.play(Create(ray_part1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(snell_color))
        
        # Show bending ray
        self.play(Create(ray_part2))
        
        # Angles and formula
        # Incident angle theta1
        arc1 = Arc(start_angle=-PI/2, angle=ray_part1.get_angle() + PI/2, radius=0.4, arc_center=p_hit, color=snell_color)
        theta1 = MathTex(r"\theta_1", color=snell_color, font_size=24)
        theta1.move_to(p_hit + UP * 0.6 + LEFT * 0.4)
        
        # Refracted angle theta2
        arc2 = Arc(start_angle=-PI/2, angle=ray_part2.get_angle() + PI/2, radius=0.4, arc_center=p_hit, color=snell_color)
        theta2 = MathTex(r"\theta_2", color=snell_color, font_size=24)
        theta2.move_to(p_hit + DOWN * 0.6 + RIGHT * 0.4)
        
        # Snell's Law equation - positioned in top right area
        snell_eq = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin \theta_1 = n_2 \sin \theta_2", color=snell_color, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(snell_eq, "A3", "A6")
        
        self.play(Create(arc1), Write(theta1))
        self.play(Create(arc2), Write(theta2))
        self.play(Write(snell_eq))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(layer_color))
        
        # Transition out Snell's Law setup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(ray_part1), FadeOut(ray_part2), FadeOut(interface), FadeOut(normal),
            FadeOut(arc1), FadeOut(theta1), FadeOut(arc2), FadeOut(theta2), FadeOut(snell_eq)
        )
        
        # Simulate layered media with decreasing refractive indices
        layers = VGroup()
        for i, row in enumerate(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]):
            rect = Rectangle(height=1.0, width=5.0, color=layer_color, stroke_width=1)
            rect.set_fill(layer_color, opacity=0.05 * (i + 1))
            self.place_in_area(rect, f"{row}1", f"{row}6")
            layers.add(rect)
            
        self.play(Create(layers))
        
        # Animate curved ray (bending toward horizontal to minimize time in lower-v/higher-n zones?)
        # "Light curves to spend more time in faster zones." 
        # If speed increases with depth (decreasing n), the ray flattens out.
        path_pts = [
            self.grid["A2"],
            self.grid["B2"] + RIGHT * 0.2,
            self.grid["C3"],
            self.grid["D4"] + RIGHT * 0.3,
            self.grid["E5"] + RIGHT * 0.4,
            self.grid["F6"]
        ]
        curved_ray = VMobject(color=ray_color)
        curved_ray.set_points_as_corners(path_pts)
        curved_ray.make_smooth()
        
        self.play(Create(curved_ray), run_time=3)
        self.wait(3)
